### J-1 `fixes_added` compares against a judged version that never holds a fix task
- quote: "at the tasks gate, the IDs of tasks under `#### Fixes` in the current `tasks.md` that the judged version doesn't hold; `[]` at every other gate."
- quote: "A file as its gate judges it: tasks.md without its `#### Fixes` sections, any other file as it is."
- quote: "text = lambda p: planned(p.name, p.read_text()) if gate == "tasks" else p.read_text()"
- quote: "Given a tasks gate where nothing was added under `#### Fixes` since the last round, when `nio jury fixcheck` and `nio jury changed` run, then their output is the same as before this change."
- situation (architecture-fit): In the existing code, `collect` stores `blob(root, text, write)` with `text = artefact(root, slug, gate)`. At the tasks gate, `artefact` passes `tasks.md` through `planned()`, which removes every `#### Fixes` section. So the judged version (`led["versions"]`, which `diff` reads back) never contains a fix task. CT-4 defines added fix tasks as those "the judged version doesn't hold", which means every fix task in `tasks.md`, including ones added before the last round. Once one fix task exists from an earlier round, AC-11's "nothing was added since the last round" case changes both the pack and the `changed` output. TC-11 doesn't catch this because its setup ("as TC-8 without T-30") has no fix tasks at all.
- fix: Have CT-4 say where the fix tasks present at the judged round come from. One option is for `collect` to record the fix task IDs it saw in the ledger next to the version, and have `fixes_added` subtract those. Add a TC where a fix task predates the last round and must not be listed.
- validation: confirmed: `artefact()` runs `tasks.md` through `planned()` at the tasks gate (jury.py:187-191), and `collect` stores that text as the judged version, so the judged version never holds a fix task. CT-4's "that the judged version doesn't hold" therefore lists every fix task in `tasks.md`, including ones added in earlier rounds, which contradicts AC-11. TC-11's setup has no fix task, so it can't catch this.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-4: collect records the Fixes IDs present at each round (led fixes); fixes_added subtracts the last round's; TC-11 now has a fix task that predates the round and must not be listed.

### J-2 The added fix task is kept out of `changed`'s list, though the ACs put it there
- quote: "prints, after its four lines, `added under Fixes: <T-n, ...>` when `fixes_added` is non-empty; nothing more otherwise."
- quote: "Observable: T-30 is in the changed list; the lenses-to-re-run list is empty."
- quote: "Assert: changed IDs `[]`, lenses to re-run `[]`, `fixes_added` `["T-30"]`."
- situation (architecture-fit): Today the CLI prints `changed: <ids>` from `jury.changed`. AC-9 says T-30 is "among the changed IDs it reports", and AC-24 says T-30 "is in the changed list". The plan instead keeps `changed:` free of T-30 and prints it on a separate fifth line. TC-20 then asserts the changed IDs are `[]`, which reads as the opposite of AC-24's observable.
- fix: Either state in CT-6 that the `added under Fixes:` line is the changed list FR-7 means, and reword TC-20's assertion to match, or add T-30 to the `changed:` line without adding any lens to re-run.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-6 states the 'added under Fixes:' line is FR-7's list; TC-20's assert reworded to match.

### J-3 CT-11 copies `tasks.md` to a run folder the tasks skill never creates
- quote: "step 3 copies `tasks.md` to the run folder before the evaluator"
- quote: "3. **Rate.** Run the `nio-evaluator` subagent on `tasks.md`. It sets every `Tier:` (with a reason) and `Effort:`."
- situation (architecture-fit): `skills/tasks/SKILL.md` never starts a run (`nio run`) or names a run folder, so "the run folder" points at nothing in the skill. The agent following step 3 has to guess where the copy goes. A copy under `.nio/specs/<slug>/` would land among the effort's own files.
- fix: Name the path in CT-11, for example `.nio/runs/<run>/tasks.before.md` after `nio run <slug>`, or a scratch path outside `.nio/specs/<slug>/`, and have step 3 say the same.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-11: step 3 runs nio run and copies to .nio/runs/<run>/tasks.before.md.

### J-4 `--rated-from`'s relation to the existing `nio check tasks` run and output is unstated
- quote: "Returns: exit 0 when every differing line pair is a `- Tier:`, `- Effort:` or `- Mode:` line and none reads `to be rated`."
- quote: "print("\n".join([f"ERROR {e}" for e in errors] + notes + [f"{len(errors)} errors"]))"
- situation (architecture-fit): The existing `nio check tasks` branch in `cli.main` always runs `tasks.check` and prints `ERROR …` lines, the estimate and an `N errors` total. CT-7 says it is like `tasks.check`, but its exit-0 rule depends only on the rating diff. Its error format (`<path>:<line>: not a rating line: …`) also has no `ERROR` prefix. The plan doesn't say whether `--rated-from` skips the normal checks or adds to them. It also doesn't say whether its errors go through the same `ERROR`/count output that skills already read.
- fix: State in CT-7 that `--rated-from` adds `rated_from`'s errors to `tasks.check`'s, printed through the existing `ERROR …`/`N errors` output, or that it replaces the normal check. Make TC-22/TC-23 assert that choice.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-7: --rated-from adds its errors to tasks.check's, printed as ERROR lines with the N errors total; TC-22 asserts it.

### J-6 TC-13 and TC-30 can pass without stripping NIO_PERF
- quote: "`NIO_PERF=1` in the test process's environment; T-1 at green."
- quote: "if not reasons and epic_closes:"
- quote: "The first claim's start of the stage (CT-5, FR-16, FR-20, FR-35, FR-36, FR-46): onto `nio/<slug>`, then the"
- situation (test-proof): `review` runs the suite only when the task closes its epic, and the setup doesn't say T-1 does. The baseline is taken at the first claim by the same `run`. If that happens in the test process with `NIO_PERF=1` set, the NIO_PERF-sensitive test is already failing at baseline. The review then counts it as `still`, not new, and passes. Either way "the review passes; T-1's attempt count is unchanged" holds on today's code, where `run` doesn't strip `NIO_PERF`.
- fix: State that T-1 is the only task of its epic, so the review runs the suite. Write the baseline line from a run without `NIO_PERF`, or with a `failing` list that excludes the test. Add a control assert: with today's `run`, that is with the env passed through, the review fails.
- validation: confirmed: The baseline comes from the same `run` (implement.py:15-27, which passes the environment through) via `suite`. With `NIO_PERF=1` in the test process, the NIO_PERF-sensitive test is already failing at baseline. `review` (implement.py:493-494) then counts it as `still`, not new, so TC-13 and TC-30 pass without the fix. The setup also doesn't say T-1 closes its epic, and `review` runs the suite only when it does (implement.py:483).
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-13: T-1 is its epic's only task; claimed with NIO_PERF unset so the baseline passes, then NIO_PERF=1 before green.

### J-7 TC-14's failing test exists at baseline, so the review counts it as old and passes
- quote: "Setup: as TC-13, with the suite's test failing on `assert 1 == 2` whatever the environment."
- quote: "Given a task whose change breaks a test's assertion"
- situation (test-proof): AC-15 is about a failure the task's change introduces. The setup has a test that fails in every environment from the start. The baseline therefore records it as failing, and `review` puts it in `still`, not in `new failures`. A correct implementation would let this review pass, so the assert "the review fails naming the failing test, and uses one attempt" fails for a reason unrelated to the AC. A bug such as `run` dropping the whole environment instead of only `NIO_PERF` would not be the thing this test checks.
- fix: Take the baseline with the test passing. Then, as T-1's change after the claim, edit the test or the code so it fails on `assert 1 == 2`, with T-1 closing its epic.
- validation: confirmed: TC-14's test fails on `assert 1 == 2` in every environment, so the baseline records it as failing. `review` classes it as `still` (implement.py:494), not under "new failures" (implement.py:495-496), so a correct implementation passes the review. That contradicts the assert "the review fails naming the failing test" and AC-15's "a failure the task's change introduces".
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-14: the test passes at baseline and T-1's change makes it fail; T-1 closes its epic.
